_source: Figma library 'Lumo.Web.Component.V1.0.Complete', read over the Figma MCP search_design_system on 2026-10-19. Verbatim component-set descriptions.

badge.desc:
Use a badge to label a status or category the user reads, not clicks — a category tag, a status pill, a "Most popular" flag.
Don’t use it for something the user can interact with; use Chip for that.

switch.desc:
Use a toggle for one setting that takes effect immediately — "Write summary with AI" in the report builder.
Don’t use it when the change needs a Save action; use Checkbox for that.

accordion.desc:
Use an accordion to let the user expand one answer at a time without leaving the page — an FAQ list on a marketing page.
Don’t use it for primary content the user needs to see without an extra click.

button.desc:
Use this component when need CTA.
Don't use it for opening external link.

card.desc:
Use a card to group related content into one surface a user can scan or act on. The card owns the surface, border, radius and padding; everything inside comes from a card layout placed in ↳Layout.
Don’t nest a card inside another card.

cardLayoutVertical.desc:
Card layout. Stacks header, body and footer down the card — the default arrangement used across Lumo screens.
Don’t use it when the card leads with an image or chart; use card/layout/horizontal.

emptyState.desc:
Use an empty state when a list, card or page has nothing to show — no results, nothing created yet, a failed load, or no permission.
Don’t leave the user without a next step; always give the action.

field.desc:
Use field to wrap any input control with a label, an optional required mark and helper or error text — used by Input, Select, Textarea and Checkbox groups alike.
Don’t write the field’s own error styling into the control; field carries it.

progress.desc:
Use progress to show how far along a measurable thing is — a score against a target, an initiative’s completion, a multi-step flow.
Don’t use it for an unknown wait; use Spinner instead.

toast.desc:
Use a toast to confirm that something happened after the user acted — saved, sent, deleted, failed — without interrupting what they are doing.
Don’t use it for anything the user must act on; that is a Modal or an Alert.
